news.title: Uefa poised to lift boycott threat after Fifa promises no World Cup sale repeat
news.lede: Uefa has received guarantees after ill-fated Infantino plan. European sides likely to go to under-20 Women’s World Cup. Uefa is poised to drop its threatened boycott of Fifa competitions after receiving concrete guarantees that the global governing body will never attempt a repeat of Gianni Infantino’s plan to sell stakes in the World Cup. The Guardian understands European teams are likely to be cleared for participation in the upcoming Under-20 Women’s World Cup, along with subsequent tournaments, after Fifa provided the binding assurances that no equivalent of its president’s ill-fated scheme will be put on the table.

news.title: UEFA to drop World Cup boycott after FIFA promise over Gianni Infantino plan
news.lede: UEFA is set to drop its boycott of FIFA competitions. It comes after football's European governing body was given guarantees that FIFA will not repeat Gianni Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup . UEFA and its 55 member associations are due to meet on Thursday ahead of the Champions League draw in Monaco where further discussions are likely to take place. UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin has been outspoken on FIFA's ill-fated plan and the English FA joined the rest to promise a boycott of future competitions which could even threaten the participation in future World Cups .

news.title: UEFA to drop FIFA boycott threat over World Cup stake plan
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino Photo: GETTY IMAGES. UEFA is set to drop its threat to boycott FIFA competitions after receiving assurances that Gianni Infantino’s controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup and other major tournaments will not be revived. The decision is expected to be confirmed at a UEFA executive committee meeting in Monaco, with European football’s governing body satisfied that its key conditions for ending the boycott threat have been met. UEFA’s 55 member associations had unanimously backed a boycott after details emerged of FIFA Forward Enterprises, a proposal that would have opened stakes in major FIFA competitions to private investors.

news.title: New book honours George Suppiah, Singapore’s first FIFA World Cup referee
news.lede: Singapore President Tharman Shanmugaratnam (2nd from left) with (from left) J. Saravana, Shamini Suppiah and Yee Whoy Chong Suppiah at the launch of George Suppiah’s biography on Aug 26. SINGAPORE – Seven-year-old Shamini Suppiah was seated on the floor of her family’s Owen Road home, glued to the black-and-white television set, surrounded by neighbours and relatives. Theirs was the only household in the neighbourhood with a TV set, and on that June 19 night in 1974, the crowd was there to watch history being made, almost 10,000km away.

news.title: Olivia Moultrie’s injury leaves the USWNT with a thinning midfield pool ahead of the World Cup
news.lede: The Portland Thorns midfielder fills a role few in the US player pool can match, and she’s in a race against time to be fit for Brazil. Olivia Moultrie is no stranger to setting her own timeline. Half a decade ago, her desire to go pro at age 15 helped change NWSL rules, which previously forbade teams from signing players under 18. The ensuing five years have seen her go from one of the country’s top prospects to a high-level midfielder, a developmental success with the Portland Thorns.

news.title: Gianni Infantino: Uefa set to drop Fifa tournament boycott threat
news.lede: Gianni Infantino has been president of Fifa since February 2016. Uefa is set to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions, having received assurances there will be no repeat of Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, BBC Sport has been told. The matter will be discussed at a meeting of Uefa's executive committee in Monaco on Thursday. Earlier this month, European football's governing body said that despite Infantino's plan being aborted following widespread condemnation, the conditions required to prevent a boycott had "not been met".

news.title: Total rift in FIFA: The South American legends who shield Infantino and defy Europe
news.lede: 'In the midst of an unprecedented institutional storm pitting Gianni Infantino against Europe's leading football governing bodies, a select group of legends of South American football has publicly come out in defense of the president of FIFA. Led by top international figures, the message seeks to cushion the harsh attacks received from the Old Continent.' The controversial clash of powers at the top of world football has reached its highest point following the call for resignation or distance put forward by European sectors in light of the governing body's recent projects. However, the response from the camp loyal to FIFA was not long in coming, seeking to uphold the figure of the Italian-Swiss executive at this critical moment.
